Did you know that today is National Black HIV/AIDS Awareness Day? 

The first National Black HIV/AIDS Awareness Day (NBHAAD) was marked in 1999 as a grassroots-education effort to raise awareness about HIV and AIDS prevention, care, and treatment in communities of color. https://t.co/KqOJziKnj7

I tested positive for COVID-19 yesterday, and I am experiencing mild symptoms. Gratefully, I am fully vaccinated and boosted. 

I encourage each person in America to get vaccinated and continue to follow the guidelines to remain safe. https://t.co/brHXGlWmfq

Why are the Republicans refusing to assist when so many of our hospitals are on the verge of closing? There is over $1 billion available in Medicaid expansion program.
https://t.co/QFvjaLvKWe

Tate Reeves continues making missteps on solving the many healthcare problems in Mississippi. 

Take the Medicaid Expansion money and help our sick hospitals.

#HealthcareinMS: We need a governor who understands that all Mississippians have the right to adequate and affordable healthcare. Mississippi has lost billions of dollars because our governors have refused to accept the money that would benefit our hospitals and communities.

Today, we celebrate the 14th Anniversary of the  #AffordableCareAct. The Biden-Harris Administration has continued to lower healthcare premiums and expand coverage for all Americans. Let us continue putting people above politics! https://t.co/Ax58tmXDOS

Today marks a milestone for rural healthcare in our district. I am glad to partner with @MSFTIssues to help rural hospitals in my district defend against rising cybersecurity attacks. Read Here: https://t.co/GYkiryWSzz https://t.co/3zU9cSGrus

Mental health is health! As we bring awareness to #worldsuicidepreventionday, take the time to check in on the people you care about.

Check out the resource below on the warning signs of a mental health condition here: https://t.co/dPn9DbVhRF #SuicidePreventionMonth https://t.co/ZFwFHr9AUC

Thank you, @NSMCenter, for inviting me to visit your nursing facility. It was great speaking to the patients and staff.  

PC: @NSMCenter https://t.co/WkgAcZ2brW

Healthcare coverage is essential! Don’t wait—research your options and sign up before the enrollment period ends on January 15, 2025! 

Your health matters.

See CMS guidance for more information.

https://t.co/RDBzYuLECu

Federal funding keeps MS02 afloat. Without it:

- Veterans lose housing assistance and jobs
- Rural hospitals lose funding
- Teachers lose jobs 
- Woman and Children lose WIC benefits 

Trump’s funding freeze is reckless and cruel.

Tonight, House Republicans voted to cut $880 billion from Medicaid, raising healthcare costs for Mississippians in order give tax breaks to billionaires. 

Because of this, nearly 664,000 Mississippians, including children, may lose essential healthcare coverage.

House Republicans want to cut $230 billion in SNAP, which would put 139,000 constituents in MS02 at risk for coverage. 

If House Republicans get their way, community programs and schools will struggle to fight food insecurity. 

This means no more school meal programs for local school districts or government assistance to help farmers provide food to local farmers' markets.

Medicaid helps 664,000 Mississippians get the care they need.

Our grandparents, moms, veterans, and kids are key groups for Medicaid coverage. If Republicans take it away, many families will struggle to stay healthy.

Healthcare should be for everyone, not just the wealthy. Medicaid matters!

Yesterday we conducted an oversight visit of Louisiana ICE facilities to demand due process and fair treatment for two detained students.

This is America - no one should be arrested or deported simply for exercising their right to free speech.
https://t.co/QIKE99vsb3

Happy Nurses Week! 

Thank you for your strength, compassion, and dedication. From hospitals to homes across Mississippi, you are the heartbeat of healthcare! https://t.co/pah62Zporg

If the GOP Tax Scam passes, 35,337 people in Mississippi’s Second Congressional District could lose their health coverage through Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act.

This means many people could suffer or even die simply because they can’t afford to see a doctor.

Today, I proudly voted against House Republicans' Big Ugly Bill. The legislation is a rip off and will make people's lives worse. 

It will raise costs, cut Medicaid, and rip food from the tables of families, including those in MS02, who rely on SNAP.

See my statement below, along with a link to the full press release:

https://t.co/d1qzSCccwo

I think this is a great video that clears up common misconceptions about Medicaid work requirements.

Take a moment to educate yourself because Republicans are not giving you all the facts!

As we celebrate National CPR and AED Awareness Week, let’s remember that CPR saves lives.

If you didn't know, most cardiac arrests happen outside of hospitals, and nearly 90% of people don’t survive.

Visit https://t.co/WCD7NAAiw0 to sign up for online or in-person training classes today. CPR can double or even triple someone’s chances of survival!

Last week, I welcomed @WhipKClark  to Mississippi’s Second District.

We toured rural hospitals threatened by House Republicans’ “Big Ugly Bill” and held a powerful town hall in Quitman County.

These stories matter and we’re bringing them back to Congress to fight for change. 

Thank you, Whip Clark.

Senate Republicans just passed the Big Ugly Bill. Now it’s back to the House where I’ll be voting NO.

This bill guts Medicaid, slashes food aid, and puts working families last so the wealthy can get more.

Mississippi deserves better. #BigUglyBill

I stood with @TheBlackCaucus on the House floor to demand protection for Medicaid and SNAP in Trump’s Big Ugly Bill.

Republicans know the truth, and they’re trying to hide it. https://t.co/FgiSA8ByqE

Veterans, their kids, their spouses, and survivors are all at risk of losing food assistance under Trump’s Big Ugly Bill. This isn’t how you thank someone for their service. 

Cutting SNAP and healthcare is a betrayal, not a policy.

Trump has already laid off thousands of federal workers, including right here in Mississippi.

If he continues to cut jobs in the military, law enforcement, healthcare, tech, and agriculture, who will be left to serve the people?

https://t.co/JZEC3uf62X
